question: After the companion revocation defect is fixed, should OpenClaw permanently support a two-layer exec denylist that overrides security=full, ask=off, and durable trust?
rationale: The code defect has a bounded repair, but only maintainers can accept the lasting configuration, protocol, upgrade, and security-policy semantics.

options.title: Adopt both layers
options.body: Keep tools.exec.denylist and exec-approvals.json denylist with shared final revocation and one-shot approvals.

options.title: Approvals file only
options.body: Keep the STOP list within the existing exec-approvals store and remove the additional runtime-config surface.

options.title: Decline denylist policy
options.body: Retain the existing deny, allowlist, and full modes without a deny-over-allow exception layer.

recommendation.title: Adopt both layers
recommendation.body: Keep tools.exec.denylist and exec-approvals.json denylist with shared final revocation and one-shot approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work and file history identify this person as the strongest available owner for the companion authorization and security-contract decision.
